title: Operation Ten-Go — the last sortie of Yamato
subtitle: East China Sea · 5–8 April 1945
footnote: Tokyo time (UTC+9). Yamato's track, the sighting and sinking positions from the combinedfleet.com TROMs (Hackett & Kingsepp), the CTF 58 action report and NHHC H-Gram 044; Kasumi and Asashimo are recorded only as '150 miles south-west of Nagasaki' and are placed approximately. Submarine tracks and Task Force 58's movements are reconstructed. Formation members are spread slightly so they don't overlap.

ships.name: Yamato
ships.sunkBy: TF 58 carrier aircraft — at least 11 torpedoes and 6 bombs

ships.name: Yahagi
ships.sunkBy: TF 58 carrier aircraft — 12 bombs and 7 torpedoes

ships.name: Hamakaze
extra: A bomb aft shears off her stern
Torpedo in No. 3 boiler room — jack-knifes and sinks

ships.name: Isokaze
extra: Near-miss floods the port engine room while she closes the stopped Yahagi
Abandoned at 19:10; sunk by Yukikaze's gunfire after her torpedo mount explodes

ships.name: Kasumi
extra: Two bomb hits and a near-miss; steering gone
Scuttled by two torpedoes from Fuyutsuki after her crew is taken off (recorded only as '150 miles SW of Nagasaki')

ships.name: Asashimo
extra: Hoists the breakdown flag — port turbine; falls astern
Alone, 20 miles behind the force, she is found first
Torpedoed by San Jacinto Avengers; sinks stern-first in five minutes — no survivors (position approximate)
ships.sunkBy: Bunker Hill and San Jacinto aircraft — lost with all hands

ships.name: Suzutsuki
extra: 500-lb bomb forward of the bridge; No. 2 turret explodes, bow blown off — 57 dead
Turns for home steaming astern at 20 knots
Arrives at Sasebo stern first; never repaired

ships.name: Fuyutsuki
extra: Two dud 5-inch rockets aboard; picks up Yamato survivors
Takes off Kasumi's crew and torpedoes her
Searches Asashimo's last position until 01:00 — nothing

ships.name: Yukikaze
extra: Picks up Yamato and Yahagi survivors, Komura and Hara among them
Embarks Isokaze's 285 survivors, then sinks her with gunfire

ships.name: Hatsushimo
extra: 257 from Hamakaze, then Yahagi's men; the only ship of the force not hit

strikes.name: Kikusui No. 1 — mass kamikaze attack
strikes.note: The first of ten Kikusui operations: about 355 kamikazes and as many escorts from Kyūshū. Destroyers Bush and Colhoun sunk at Radar Picket Station 1, Emmons wrecked, some twenty other ships hit. Ten-Go is meant to sail under its cover

strikes.name: Air cover — 203rd Air Group Zeros
strikes.note: Fourteen Zeros in relays are all Ugaki's 5th Air Fleet can spare; the cover is gone by 10:00 — as US radio intelligence already knows

strikes.name: Yamato's last floatplane
strikes.note: The Jake searches ahead of the force and flies on to Kyūshū

strikes.name: Kamikazes on TF 58
strikes.note: Four attack the carriers while the strike is away; one hits Hancock's flight deck — 62 killed, 71 wounded. Maryland and Bennett are hit off Okinawa the same day

strikes.name: Dawn search — Essex Hellcats
strikes.note: Forty Hellcats in fours cover the sectors 336°–056° to 325 miles; an Essex team finds the force at 08:23 and shadows it

strikes.name: VPB-21 Mariners
strikes.note: Two Mariners from the tender Chandeleur at Kerama Retto hold contact for four hours and home the strike in; Yamato's 18-inch sanshikidan shells fail to drive them off. They later land to pick up a downed crew

strikes.name: First wave — TG 58.1 and 58.3
strikes.note: Hornet, Bennington, Belleau Wood, San Jacinto, Essex, Bunker Hill, Bataan, Cabot — 280 launched, Hancock's 53 fail to join. Two bombs and a torpedo on Yamato, Hamakaze sunk, Yahagi stopped, Suzutsuki's bow blown off

strikes.name: Hancock air group
strikes.note: Launched fifteen minutes late, never finds the target

strikes.name: Asashimo hunted down
strikes.note: Bunker Hill Helldivers stop the straggler at 12:45; San Jacinto's Avengers finish her at 13:05 — Asashimo goes down with all 326 men

strikes.name: Second wave — Essex and Bataan
strikes.note: Fifty aircraft work over the stopped Yahagi and the destroyers around her

strikes.name: Third wave — TG 58.4
strikes.note: Yorktown, Intrepid, Langley: torpedoes concentrated on Yamato's port side — three at 13:33, more at 14:07 and 14:17; three bombs at 14:02. She capsizes at 14:20. US losses for the day: 10 aircraft, 12 men

One hit in No. 3 boiler room; Hamakaze breaks in two

Yahagi has now taken seven torpedoes and twelve bombs
Three hits port side; counter-flooding fails to check the list

ports.name: Kure
ports.note: Kure Naval Arsenal, Yamato's builder; the fleet dispersed from here after the 19 March carrier raid

ports.name: Tokuyama
ports.note: Navy fuel depot — Yamato takes on 3,400 tons on 6 April

ports.name: Sasebo
ports.note: The surviving destroyers land some 1,600 survivors here on 8 April; Suzutsuki arrives stern first

ports.name: Kanoya
ports.note: 5th Air Fleet's main kamikaze base; Kikusui No. 1 flies from here and its satellite fields

ports.name: Kasanohara
ports.note: 203rd Air Group — the fourteen Zeros that covered Yamato until 10:00

ports.name: Okinawa (Hagushi)
ports.note: The invasion beaches of 1 April — Yamato's objective

ports.name: Kerama Retto
ports.note: Seized 26 March as the fleet's anchorage; seaplane tender Chandeleur's Mariners fly from here

ports.name: Hiyoshi — Combined Fleet HQ
ports.note: Admiral Toyoda's underground headquarters at Keio University, from which Ten-Go was ordered

ports.name: Kanoya — 5th Air Fleet HQ
ports.note: Vice Admiral Ugaki's headquarters for the Kikusui operations

ports.name: Guam — CINCPAC / COMSUBPAC
ports.note: Nimitz's advanced headquarters; Threadfin's and Hackleback's contact reports come here and go straight to Spruance

rescues.note: Hatsushimo takes 257 of Hamakaze's crew, her captain among them
Yukikaze and Hatsushimo rescue 555, including Komura and Hara; 446 lost
Fuyutsuki, Yukikaze and Hatsushimo find only 269 of Yamato's 3,332 in the oil; Rear Admiral Morishita is the senior survivor
Kasumi's crew, her captain included, taken off before she is torpedoed
Isokaze's 285 survivors, ComDesDiv 17 among them, embark before Yukikaze sinks her
The bowless Suzutsuki picks up a few men before turning for home

yamato.name: Vice Admiral Seiichi Itō
yamato.role: Commander, Second Fleet — Surface Special Attack Force
yamato.bio: A former vice-chief of the Naval General Staff who opposed the sortie as a pointless waste of 4,000 lives until told it was 'a fitting opportunity to die'. Once committed he led it without illusion, and at 14:02 ordered the survivors to abandon ship and rescue the swimmers rather than fight on.
yamato.fate: Shook hands with his staff and went down with Yamato, 7 April 1945; posthumously Admiral.

yahagi.name: Rear Admiral Keizō Komura
yahagi.bio: Commanded the escort of one light cruiser and eight destroyers. Yahagi's captain, Tameichi Hara, whose memoir is the classic account of the day, told his crew: 'We are not going to die in vain.' Yahagi took twelve bombs and seven torpedoes.
yahagi.fate: Rescued with Hara by Hatsushimo and Yukikaze; survived the war.

tf58.name: Vice Admiral Marc A. Mitscher
tf58.bio: Captain of Hornet at Midway three years earlier, now commanding fifteen fast carriers. Warned overnight by the submarines and the codebreakers, he launched everything at 10:00 without waiting for the search to confirm, and only then told Spruance — who had meant to let his battleships do it.

tf54.name: Rear Admiral Morton L. Deyo
tf54.role: Commander, Task Force 54 (Gunfire and Covering Force)
tf54.bio: Spruance's first instinct was to give Yamato to the old battleships; Deyo planned a night gun action with six battleships, seven cruisers and 21 destroyers. Mitscher's aircraft made it academic.

threadfin.name: Cdr John J. Foote
threadfin.bio: Sighted the force clearing Bungo Suido and, ordered to report before attacking, sent the contact that put the whole Fifth Fleet on notice — and lost his chance to shoot.
